scenarioStory.history: Police were called after bystanders reported a man running through traffic, yelling incoherently, and tearing off his clothes. On EMS arrival, law enforcement has him in handcuffs; he continues to struggle violently, is drenched in sweat, and is not answering questions coherently. Bystanders report he appeared to be using drugs earlier at a nearby party.
scenarioStory.course: Initial Contact: Crew arrives to find a 29-year-old male in police custody, combative, hyperthermic, diaphoretic, and incoherent, consistent with excited delirium likely from stimulant intoxication. → Sedation given, safe restraint applied: Crew administers ketamine for rapid sedation, ensures the patient is restrained safely (supine or lateral, never prone or hobbled, chest wall unrestricted), and immediately places a cardiac monitor given the known risk of sudden arrest in excited delirium. → Active cooling initiated for hyperthermia: With the patient sedated and monitored, the crew initiates active cooling for the core temperature above 104°F and establishes IV access for cool fluid boluses, prioritizing cooling given the risk of severe heat-related organ injury. → Improving, monitored closely for transport: With active cooling, fluids, and sedation on board, the patient's vital signs trend toward normal. The crew maintains continuous cardiac monitoring throughout transport, remaining alert for sudden deterioration.

patientInformation.patientName: Unknown Male (later identified as Marcus Boyd)
patientInformation.patientCondition: Combative, agitated male, bystanders report bizarre behavior and disrobing in public

scenarioEvents.name: Initial Contact
scenarioEvents.description: Crew arrives to find a 29-year-old male in police custody, combative, hyperthermic, diaphoretic, and incoherent, consistent with excited delirium likely from stimulant intoxication.

scenarioEvents.name: Sedation given, safe restraint applied
scenarioEvents.description: Crew administers ketamine for rapid sedation, ensures the patient is restrained safely (supine or lateral, never prone or hobbled, chest wall unrestricted), and immediately places a cardiac monitor given the known risk of sudden arrest in excited delirium.
relatedChecklist: Ketamine 320 mg IM (80 kg × 4 mg/kg), 3-5 minute onset expected
Restrain supine with extremities individually secured to the stretcher frame; never prone, never hobbled, chest wall unrestricted
Apply cardiac monitor immediately given known risk of sudden cardiopulmonary arrest

scenarioEvents.name: Active cooling initiated for hyperthermia
scenarioEvents.description: With the patient sedated and monitored, the crew initiates active cooling for the core temperature above 104°F and establishes IV access for cool fluid boluses, prioritizing cooling given the risk of severe heat-related organ injury.
relatedChecklist: Begin active cooling (evaporative/tarp-assisted) — avoid wet cloths, continue until temp under 102.2°F or mental status improves
Establish IV access; give cool isotonic fluid bolus 1600 mL (80 kg × 20 mL/kg)

scenarioEvents.name: Improving, monitored closely for transport
scenarioEvents.description: With active cooling, fluids, and sedation on board, the patient's vital signs trend toward normal. The crew maintains continuous cardiac monitoring throughout transport, remaining alert for sudden deterioration.
relatedChecklist: Continuously reassess airway, breathing, circulation, and extremity perfusion in restraints throughout transport

scenarioEvents.name: Prone or hobbled restraint used
scenarioEvents.description: The patient is restrained prone with hands and feet secured behind the back. Combined with his hyperthermia and physical exhaustion, this significantly increases his risk of positional asphyxia and sudden cardiopulmonary arrest.
relatedChecklist: Immediately reposition supine or lateral, remove hobble restraint, reassess airway and breathing
